q: 1. The durability of concrete is due to its resistance to
explain: Durability of concrete is defined by its overall ability to resist deterioration from a combination of environmental exposure, internal disruptive forces, and chemical attack/cracking.

q: 2. In concrete, use of angular crushed aggregate in place of natural rounded gravel affects
explain: as per book c.Angular crushed aggregate provides better mechanical interlock and bond with the cement matrix, which particularly improves the flexural tensile strength of the concrete.

q: 3. Concrete can take tension up to
options: 10% of the compressive strength of steel
10% of the combined compressive strength of concrete & R/F
10% of the total tensile strength of the section
explain: Concrete's tensile strength is generally only about 10% of its own compressive strength, reflecting its characteristic weakness in tension relative to compression.

q: 4. The compressive strength of an ordinary Portland cement cube after 7 days test should not be less than
explain: As per IS 269 specifications, the minimum 7-day compressive strength requirement for OPC mortar cubes is 17.5 N/mm².

q: 5. The ratio of various ingredients (cement, sand, aggregates) in concrete of grade M 200, is
explain: The nominal mix proportion associated with grade M200 concrete (equivalent to M20 in modern notation) is 1 : 1.5 : 3 (cement : sand : coarse aggregate).

q: 6. The cube strength of concrete exceeds the cylinder strength by (in percent)
explain: Due to the difference in specimen geometry and the resulting confinement/end effects during testing, cube strength typically exceeds cylinder strength by about 20 to 25%.

q: 7. For cylindrical specimens, the dimension of cylinder generally used
explain: The standard cylindrical test specimen used for compressive strength testing has a diameter of 15 cm and a height of 30 cm, giving the standard height-to-diameter ratio of 2.

q: 8. Cube test is used to determine
explain: The standard cube test is specifically designed to determine the compressive strength of concrete, the most commonly required strength parameter.

q: 9. For cylindrical specimens, minimum strength required should be
options: 0.20 times the strength of 15 cm cubes
0.40 times the strength of 15 cm cubes
0.60 times the strength of 15 cm cubes
0.80 times the strength of 15 cm cubes
explain: The compressive strength obtained from a standard cylinder is typically about 0.80 times the strength of an equivalent 15 cm cube, due to the difference in specimen shape and testing conditions.

q: 10. The surface area of standard cube used for finding compressive strength of concrete is
explain: The standard cube face is 15cm x 15cm = 225 cm² = 22500 mm² = 0.0225 m² - all these are equivalent expressions of the same area in different units, so all of the above is correct.

q: 11. During application of load on cylindrical specimen the failure plane makes an angle of .........with the horizontal.
explain: Under compressive load, cylindrical concrete specimens typically fail along a shear plane inclined at approximately 60 degrees to the horizontal (or about 30 degrees to the vertical axis of loading).

q: 12. The ultimate load of a balanced reinforced concrete beam is proportional to
options: crushing strength of concrete and/or tensile strength of the steel
explain: In a balanced section, both the concrete's crushing (compressive) strength and the steel's tensile strength reach their limiting values simultaneously, so the ultimate load depends on both.

q: 13. The grade of concrete M 150 means that compressive strength of 15 cm cube after 28 days is
explain: By definition, the grade designation M150 directly specifies a characteristic compressive strength of 150 kg/cm² for a 15cm cube tested after 28 days.

q: 14. The test conducted in the labouratory on the specimen made out of trial concrete mix is called
explain: A preliminary test is carried out in the laboratory on specimens made from trial concrete mixes to establish suitable proportions before actual construction begins.

q: 15. Allowable shear strength of concrete, depends upon
explain: The allowable shear strength of concrete is generally derived as a function of, and depends upon, its compressive strength, as per design code provisions.

q: 16. The strength of concrete is decreased by
explain: Excessive vibration (over-vibration), impact loading, and fatigue (repeated cyclic loading) can all contribute to a decrease in the effective strength of concrete over time.

q: 17. The most appropriate method to specify the concrete mix is by
explain: Specifying concrete by its grade (e.g., M20, M25) is considered the most appropriate and standardized method, as it directly denotes the required characteristic compressive strength.

q: 18. The total number of grades of ordinary concrete stipulated in IS 456:2000 are
explain: IS 456:2000 stipulates a total of 6 grades under the ordinary concrete category (M10, M15, M20, M25, M30... within the ordinary grade group).

q: 19. The standard size of a concrete cube for compressive strength test is
explain: The standard concrete cube specimen size used for compressive strength testing is 150 mm x 150 mm x 150 mm (15 cm cube).

q: 20. If the various concrete ingredients i.e. cement, sand and aggregates are in the ratio of 1:3:6, the grade of concrete, is
explain: The nominal mix ratio 1:3:6 corresponds to the M150 grade of concrete as per standard grade-mix ratio correlations.

q: 21. Permissible compressive strength of M150 concrete grade is
explain: As indicated by its designation, the M150 grade of concrete has a characteristic (permissible) compressive strength of 150 kg/cm².

q: 22. Permissible compressive strength of M150 concrete grade is
explain: 150 kg/cm² is equivalent to approximately 15 N/mm² (since 1 N/mm² ≈ 10.2 kg/cm²), making 15 N/mm² the correct equivalent expression of the M150 grade strength.

q: 23. Permissible compressive strength of M200 concrete grade is
explain: By definition, the M200 grade concrete has a characteristic (permissible) compressive strength of 200 kg/cm².

q: 24. The ratio of various ingredients (cement, sand, aggregates) in concrete of grade M 200, is
explain: The M200 grade of concrete typically corresponds to a nominal mix ratio of 1:1.5:3 (cement:sand:aggregate).

q: 25. Permissible compressive strength of M250 concrete grade is
explain: By definition, the M250 grade concrete has a characteristic (permissible) compressive strength of 250 kg/cm².

q: 26. Permissible compressive strength of M300 concrete grade is
explain: By definition, the M300 grade concrete has a characteristic (permissible) compressive strength of 300 kg/cm².

q: 27. The concrete mixes are designated into
explain: As per the classification used in this text (older IS 456 provisions), concrete mixes are designated into seven standard grades.

q: 28. Which of the following grade is not recommended by IS 456:1978
explain: M55 grade is not among the standard grades listed/recommended under the (older) IS 456:1978 provisions referenced in this text.

q: 29. The test conducted in the laboratory on the specimen made out of trial concrete mix is called
explain: A preliminary test is a laboratory test performed on trial mix specimens to determine and finalize the mix design before actual site work begins.

q: 30. In preliminary test, the concrete is placed in the mould in ......... layers of equal volume.
explain: As per standard cube/cylinder casting procedure for preliminary tests, concrete is placed and compacted in three equal layers.

q: 31. The preliminary test should be repeated if the difference of compressive strength of three test specimen exceeds.
explain: As per the acceptance criteria in this text, if the compressive strength results of the three test specimens vary by more than 1.5 N/mm², the preliminary test must be repeated.

q: 32. The factors which affects the design of concrete mix is
explain: Concrete mix design is influenced jointly by aggregate fineness modulus, water-cement ratio, and required workability (slump) — hence all of these factors are relevant.

q: 33. For the construction of RCC slab, column, beam and walls, the minimum grade of concrete mixed is used for
explain: The minimum recommended nominal mix for general RCC construction (slabs, columns, beams, walls) is 1:2:4, corresponding to M15 grade concrete.

q: 34. M100 grade of concrete approximates
explain: The M100 grade of concrete (lowest strength grade) approximately corresponds to a lean nominal mix ratio of 1:3:6.

q: 35. The number of bags of cement required per cubic meter of 1:2:4 concrete will be approximately
explain: For a nominal 1:2:4 concrete mix, standard calculations show that approximately 4 to 5 bags of cement (50 kg each) are needed per cubic metre of concrete.

q: 36. M150 grade of concrete approximates
explain: The M150 grade of concrete approximately corresponds to a nominal mix ratio of 1:2:4 (cement:sand:aggregate).

q: 37. The increase in strength of concrete after 6 months
explain: As per the strength-gain data referenced in this text, concrete strength increases by about 20% beyond the 28-day value after 6 months of curing.

q: 38. To determine modulus of rupture, the size of test specimen used is
explain: As per IS 516, the standard flexural (modulus of rupture) test beam specimen size is 150 × 150 × 700 mm.

q: 39. Workability of concrete is directly proportional to
explain: Well-graded aggregate reduces void content and improves the flow characteristics of the mix, thereby directly improving workability.

q: 40. The relation between modulus of rupture fcr and characteristic strength fck is given by
explain: As per IS 456, the flexural strength (modulus of rupture) of concrete is related to its characteristic compressive strength by fcr = 0.7√fck.

q: 41. The compressive strength of 100 mm cube as compared to 150 mm cube is always
explain: Due to the size effect in concrete testing, smaller 100 mm cube specimens generally record a higher apparent compressive strength than standard 150 mm cubes.

q: 42. The modulus of elasticity E of concrete can be taken as
explain: As per IS 456, the static modulus of elasticity of concrete is commonly estimated using the empirical formula E = 5700√fck (in N/mm²).

q: 43. The concrete mix which causes difficulty in obtaining a smooth finish, possess
explain: A harsh concrete mix, characterized by excessive hardness/lack of fines, makes it difficult to achieve a smooth surface finish.

q: 44. The top diameter, bottom diameter, and the height of slump mould are
explain: As per IS 1199, the standard slump cone mould has a top diameter of 10 cm, bottom diameter of 20 cm, and a height of 30 cm.

q: 45. If the slump of concrete mix is 60 mm, its workability is
explain: A slump value of 60 mm falls within the medium workability range according to the standard slump classification table.

q: 46. In slump test, each layer of concrete is compacted by a steel rod 60 cm long and 16 m diameter for ......
explain: As per IS 1199, each of the three layers in the slump test mould is tamped 25 times using the standard 16 mm diameter, 60 cm long steel rod.

q: 47. The grade of concrete not recommended by IS 456 is
explain: As per the classification referenced in this text, M30 does not appear among the listed standard grades recommended by IS 456.

q: 48. The grade of concrete M150 means that compressive strength of a 15 cm cube after 28 days is
explain: In the older grade-naming convention (M followed by a number in kg/cm²), M150 directly denotes a 28-day cube compressive strength of 150 kg/cm².

q: 49. According to IS 456, the number of grades of concrete mix is
explain: As per the classification referenced in this text (older IS 456 provisions), concrete mixes are designated into seven standard grades.

q: 50. If the engineer in charge approves the 10 cm cubes may be used for the work test of concrete provided maximum nominal size of aggregate, does not exceed
explain: Smaller 10 cm cube specimens can only be used for testing when the maximum nominal aggregate size is limited to 20 mm, ensuring the specimen dimensions remain proportionate to the largest aggregate particle.
